name: Aretas
overview: Aretas was a male king who ruled as the ethnarch over Damascus, as identified in 2 Corinthians 11:32. The biblical record does not specify his tribal affiliation or provide additional personal details. His role as a ruler in Damascus places him in the context of the New Testament narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Aretas appears once in Scripture without a given meaning or divine origin. It is presented simply as a proper name in 2 Corinthians 11:32, without further explanation of its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Aretas beyond his position as king over the ethnarch in Damascus. No other relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Aretas is significant in the New Testament as a political figure who held authority in Damascus during the time of the early church. His mention in 2 Corinthians highlights the historical context of Paul's ministry and the challenges faced by early Christians. Although details are sparse, Aretas's rule is part of the backdrop against which the apostolic mission unfolded.
